01 - The shift

From answers to agents

Then - ask and copy
You asked a chatbot for text, copied it, and did the real work yourself. The AI was a smart typewriter.

Now - delegate and review
You describe an outcome. An agent plans, executes across tools, and reports back with evidence. Your job shifts to direction, review and judgment.

Quality now depends on how well you brief, check and correct.

02 - The toolbox, 1 of 3

Agents write the code

Reads a codebase, edits files, runs commands, works with git: branches, commits, pull requests. Reach for it to delegate well-scoped coding tasks and review the diffs.[1]
Coding agentClaude CodeDelegate a task, review the diff
OpenAI's coding partner for well-scoped engineering tasks - bugs, refactors, features - designed for multi-agent workflows where several tasks run in parallel.[2]
Coding agentCodexParallel tasks, one queue
An AI-first code editor: delegate the implementation and keep your attention on direction and review.[3]
AI editorCursorYou steer, it types

Assistants you just text

Works where you already talk - WhatsApp or iMessage. You text a request like you would to a person; it researches, drafts, builds and reports back, checking with you before acting. This site was briefed by WhatsApp message.
Personal assistantInstinctText it like a person
A personal-assistant bot - the class saw creator Vlad Tansky's walkthrough of building and running a product from his phone with it.[9]
Personal assistantGrok BotA bot that runs your day
OpenAI's always-on personal agents inside ChatGPT - built to keep handling your ongoing work in the background.[8]

04 - The actual prompts

Real prompts, typos included

05 - Rules of the loop

Workflow, not gambling

Sources or it didn't happen. Verification is your job.
Disclose the AI. Professionalism, not confession.
Review before scale. Never mass-produce what you haven't inspected.
The human owns the decision. Budgets, sends and merges stay with you.
06 - Your turn

Run the same loop for your clip

1Brief - one message: audience, country, three cultural points, tone, length.
2Research - credible sources first; paste them into your prompt.
3Prototype - generate a first clip with a video tool. Expect it to be wrong.
4Critique and revise - list exactly what is off. Two or three loops is normal.
5Verify and disclose - check claims, watch the final render, add an AI-use note.

Attribution: this assignment workflow follows the course's "same loop" asset method (Oded Sharon, 2025), applied here to the clip you will produce.
